Recursive dynamic programme over axis-aligned layouts: split a square into an m×m grid and give each cell its own sub-layout (with an optional merged j×j block or several 1-square blocks), with spare squares as size-0 points. The best layout for every count up to n is found by DP and then rebuilt.

Integer-grid guillotine DP: for each grid resolution m, compute the best sum of sides using at most c squares in an a×b rectangle by max-plus combination of vertical and horizontal cuts (vectorised in numpy). It then reconstructs the best layout over all m tried, within a time budget.

Build an m×m grid, merge t disjoint 2×2 blocks into single larger squares, and drop d cells to size zero so the count fits. This keeps the total sum (m² − 2t − d)/m with at most n squares. Search all m and t for the best sum, and pad with zero-size squares.

Tile a K×K integer grid with axis-aligned squares of integer sizes.
